newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt militants urge army to overthrow government.
newsitem.headline: Egypt militants urge army to overthrow government.

text.p: An Egyptian Moslem militant group that assassinated president Anwar Sadat during a military parade 15 years ago, urged the armed forces on Sunday to overthrow the "apostate regime" of his successor President Hosni Mubarak.
Vanguards of Conquest, a revival of the Jihad (Holy Struggle) Group that killed Sadat, slammed the Cairo government for being "an agent that rules Egypt for the sake of the Americans and the Jews".
The group made the comments in a statement faxed to an international news agency on the anniversary of Egypt's war with Israel in 1973, which Egyptians say ended with a victory for their country.
"October 6, 1973, was a victory over the sons of monkeys and pigs. October 6, 1981, was the day of assassination of the pharaoh of Egypt, the damned Sadat," the group said.

"The agent Sadat sold at a cheap price your victories of October, 1973, by signing the treaty of surrender that he was dragged into and which is now being implemented by his successor the agent Mubarak," the group added.

Sadat became the first Arab leader to sign a peace treaty with Israel in 1979. He was killed by militant army officers who were members of Jihad during a military parade on October 6, 1981 and succeeded by his vice president, Hosni Mubarak.

"Be patient and struggle for the sake of raising God's word by overthrowing this agent regime," Vanguards of Conquest said in the statement, entitled "A Message to our united brothers in the Egyptian armed forces".

Several army officers were hanged for their role in Sadat's assassination, Jihad was smashed and military security has kept a close eye on the armed forces ever since for any hint of militant infiltration.
But Jihad resurfaced under its new guise as the Vanguards of Conquest with a bang in 1993 when it tried to blow up former prime minister Atef Sedki and Interior Minister Hassan al-Alfi.

Also that year, army officers were on the charge sheet again when three of them were among 53 militants of Vanguards of Conquest accused of plotting to overthrow the government in the first such case against army personnel since Sadat's murder.
Two army officers were executed by a shooting squad in 1994 for plotting to kill Mubarak by laying explosives on an airfield he uses near the border with Libya.
More than 1,000 people have been killed in Egypt since Moslem militants launched a bloody campaign in 1992 to overthrow Mubarak's government and set up a strict Islamic state.

"This apostate regime thinks you are its servants and slaves. But the nation will see by your actions that you are slaves of God only...Do not obey the oppressors and do not heed their orders and free yourselves of the crimes of the regime," Vanguards of Conquest told the armed forces.

The group also slammed the Cairo government for "overseeing the treaties of betrayal, humiliation, and surrender", in a reference to Egypt's role as mediator in peace talks between Israel and its Arab neighbours.
It also condemned Palestinian President Yasser Arafat for trying to make peace with Israel and "ruling Gaza for the sake of the Jews".

"He (Arafat) is humiliated and begs for peace from the Jews. (Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu will impose his policies and plans, which include expanding settlements and plundering and confiscating Palestinian land. He has made Arafat the mayor of Gaza and Jericho," the group said.
